newsitem.title: UK: North Sea quiet, outright price moves on OPEC news.
newsitem.headline: North Sea quiet, outright price moves on OPEC news.

text.p: North Sea crude differentials held steady in quiet trade on Thursday as outright values swayed in reaction to news from the OPEC meeting in Vienna.
Crude traders doubted that members of the 11-nation cartel would keep their pledge to cut back chronic over-production to agreed quota levels.
That doubt was reflected in outright values on the IPE August contract, which lost 27 cents by 1230 GMT to $17.95.
The contract had shot up 35 cents yesterday after OPEC announced a "firm" committment to respect output ceilings.
"It's now fallen back a bit and I don't think people are paying too much attention to Vienna," said one trader.
"Talk is cheap and the important thing is that they haven't introduced any measures to punish over-producers, so there is no incentive to really cut back," he added.
OPEC members currently pump out 2 million barrels per day above the agreed limit of 25.03 million bpd. OPEC oil ministers agreed on Thursday to freeze the figure for six months.
Cash crude markets tracked the ups and downs of the outright price, firming in the morning to catch up with late Brent futures gains, before softening as doubt over the OPEC deal crept back in.
After healthy activity in North Sea grades on Wednesday afternoon physical market talk was muted, with some players away at industry functions.
Dealers believed a Brent cargo moved from a trader to a major equity holder on Wednesday at August Brent -25 cents, after being offered at -10 and -20 cents on the two previous days.
The deal, if confirmed, represents a slight fall from an early week price of August -19 cents, but was described as still quite healthy.
North Sea crude demand was described as still healthy, and with most of the first two decades of July cleared out, attention was shifting to end-month cargoes.
The reputed Brent buyer was also heard to have bought a short-term swap for the week after next against August. He was heard to have paid -35 cents but to be reoffering it at the same number.
An August/September inter-month spread was done at -17 cents.

In the Mediterranean Urals was holding on to its strong numbers, with most first half July cargoes already committed to end-users and Iraqi barrels, the usual sour alternative, not predicted to appear before the middle of next month.
A Urals cargo was rumoured traded on Wednesday at numbers "in the 70's" but this could not be confirmed.
